turn.subject: trial-times
turn.user_message: A normal Tuesday: doctors decide anywhere from 6 to 9 PM, depending on the consultant. They sign around 11. Papers ready 12:30, bill final 1:30, insurance approves around 2:30, patient leaves 3:15, bed ready 4:30.

text: Your real times change the picture a little, and mostly in a useful way. Two of my guesses held up. One was wrong in a way that helps.
The decision time isn’t fixed. It moves with each consultant. So the trial should start with the consultants who decide latest, because their patients lose the most of the evening.
chat.invite: Shall I update the trial plan with these times?
chat.note: The latest decisions lose the most time.

blocks.title: One normal day, step by step

blocks.caption: Your normal Tuesday, on the same timeline.

items.title: Doctors decide 6 to 9 PM
items.text: Not a fixed 7 PM. It depends on the consultant.
more_points: The unused hours overnight are 14 to 17, not 16.
Patients of late deciders get the least time to prepare.
The trial should start with those consultants.

items.title: Papers take 1½ hours
more_points: This is the typing step the software removes.
It was the biggest hold-up I expected, and your times agree.

items.title: Bed ready 75 minutes later
items.text: New: the bed sits empty after leaving.
more_points: Part of this may be waiting for housekeeping to be told.
The trial will time when housekeeping is told, not just the cleaning.
